To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the time delay of the hydrodynamic expansion due to the presence of a finite width, Δ T ~ 0.1T c, of the QGP-hadronic transition region is a rather robust feature of relativistic heavy-ion collisions, (2) the time delay is likely to be maximal around RHIC energies, and (3) the time-delay signal can be enhanced by a factor of 3 or so by using a longitudinal boost-invariant geometry.

(1) The time-delay signature of the formation of a quark-gluón plasma in heavy ion collisions is robust with respect to uncertainties in the width, ∆T, of the transition between quark-glon plasma and hadron gas.

(i) the pion-interference correlation functions in ultrarelativistic heavy ion collisions are very sensitive to the width of the quark-gluonic plasma phase transition, (ii) the ratio of inverse widths in side- and out-directions is enhanced for time-delayed hydrodynamic expansion, (iii) the enhancement is robust against uncertainties in ΔT, and (iv) the signal is likely maximized at RHIC energies.
